report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/mint.py (lines 281-570): verified _show, _read_worktree, _resolve_sha, _short_hash, MUST_INCLUDE_CAP, _diff_magnitude, _diffed_symbols, _in_scope_modules, and the core of _mint_from_diffs; all docstring claims in this window are kept; no broken claims found; several invariants and edge behaviors noted.
risks: _mint_from_diffs | medium | anchor_pool fallback to per_file when existing is empty: if a deleted file (after_text None) is the only per_file entry and it is not floor-tripped, it can become the anchor, contradicting the docstring's 'still EXISTS after the edit' requirement. | Add a test where all changed files are deleted and assert no anchor is chosen or that a deleted file is explicitly excluded from anchor_pool.

_mint_from_diffs | medium | _diffed_symbols uses extract_units with before_text or '' and after_text or '', substituting empty string for None; this makes a deleted file's before_units empty and a created file's after_units empty, matching the intent, but the empty string is also a valid empty file; a deleted file and an empty file are indistinguishable in _diffed_symbols. | Confirm whether extract_units can distinguish between an empty file and a missing file; if needed, pass None explicitly or add a test for empty-file vs deleted-file behavior.

_mint_from_diffs | medium | The cross_file_sizes loop skips anchor and floor-tripped files but does not skip files whose rel_lang is None (unsupported extension) before the language-family check; such files contribute to labels_filtered_cross_language, which is fine, but the comment 'JUNK / CROSS-LANGUAGE / SECRET-FLOOR filtering ... happens per (file, name) occurrence' is upheld. | No action needed unless a file with spec None and a non-junk name is expected to be filtered by cross-language; current behavior is consistent.

_mint_from_diffs | low | The anchor selection uses sorted(anchor_pool, key=lambda r: (-len(anchor_pool[r]), r))[0]; this is deterministic but ties are broken by path string, which is fine. However, if anchor_pool contains a deleted file (when existing is empty), the anchor may be a deleted file, violating the docstring. | See first risk; add a regression test for all-deleted scenario.

_mint_from_diffs | low | The MUST_INCLUDE_CAP comment says '~25 keeps a minted task's label set in the same ballpark as the hand-picked tasks in tasks.py'; this is a policy justification and not directly verifiable from this chunk, but the cap is applied as `ranked[:MUST_INCLUDE_CAP]` and `dropped = len(ranked) - len(kept)`; the cap is enforced. | No action needed.

_mint_from_diffs | low | The diagnostics dict is built with 'skipped_out_of_scope' always present, but 'skipped_secret_floor' is added unconditionally after the floor check; if no floor-tripped files, it is empty list. The docstring does not explicitly promise 'skipped_secret_floor' always present, but it is. | No action needed.
todos: Add a test for _mint_from_diffs when all changed files are deleted (existing empty) to verify anchor selection does not pick a deleted file.
Add a test for _mint_from_diffs when a file's after_text is None but before_text is non-empty (deleted file) to ensure _diffed_symbols treats it as a pure remove and that the anchor pool excludes it.
Add a test for _mint_from_diffs when cross_file_sizes becomes empty after filtering to verify the diagnostics reason and that no task is minted.
Add a test for _mint_from_diffs when the anchor file is floor-tripped but other files are not, to verify the anchor pool excludes floor-tripped files.
Add a test for _diffed_symbols with duplicate symbol names across sibling classes to verify the magnitude is the max and that both occurrences are considered.

handoff.purpose: Implements diff-based symbol extraction and the core minting logic for aggregate tasks, including scope filtering, floor-tripping, label hygiene, and cap ranking.

symbols.name: _show
symbols.note: Returns blob contents of rel at ref via git show, or None if the path did not exist (git show fails).

symbols.name: _read_worktree
symbols.note: Reads current on-disk contents of rel, returning None on OSError (deleted file).

symbols.name: _resolve_sha
symbols.note: Resolves a ref to a full SHA via git rev-parse, stripping whitespace; returns None if git command returns empty.

symbols.name: _short_hash
symbols.note: Computes a 12-character SHA-256 hash of the repr of all parts, separated by null bytes.

symbols.name: MUST_INCLUDE_CAP
symbols.note: Ceiling on the number of must_include labels; set to 25.

symbols.name: _diff_magnitude
symbols.note: Counts +/- lines in a unified diff between joined before/after source lists, excluding file headers; used for ranking only.

symbols.name: _diffed_symbols
symbols.note: Returns a dict of symbol name to diff magnitude for symbols whose extracted source differs, handling duplicate names by matching against sorted source lists; returns {} for unsupported file types.

symbols.name: _in_scope_modules
symbols.note: Returns a frozenset of module paths from the cached index; returns empty frozenset on any exception.

symbols.name: _mint_from_diffs
symbols.note: Builds one aggregate task from file diffs, scoped and cross-file labeled; returns (task, diagnostics).

claims.text: Blob contents of ``rel`` at ``ref``, or ``None`` if it didn't exist there (distinct from an empty-but-present file, which is a real "").
claims.why: The function returns _git(...) which is None on failure (per _git's contract) and the actual blob content otherwise; an empty file would yield an empty string, not None.

claims.text: Current on-disk contents of ``rel``, or ``None`` if it's gone (deleted by the edit being minted).
claims.why: The function catches OSError and returns None; otherwise it reads the file with errors='replace'.

claims.text: Ceiling on must_include -- see _mint_from_diffs for the ranking/drop rule.
claims.why: The constant is defined and later used in _mint_from_diffs at line ~570 as ranked[:MUST_INCLUDE_CAP].

claims.text: Deterministic size proxy for one symbol, used only to rank which labels survive MUST_INCLUDE_CAP -- NOT a precision diff.
claims.why: The function counts +/- lines in a unified diff with n=0, which is a deterministic but coarse measure; it is used only for ranking in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: Counts the +/- lines in a unified diff between the joined before/after source blocks (before_srcs/after_srcs are lists because a name can repeat across sibling classes/closures -- see _diffed_symbols).
claims.why: The function joins the lists with newlines, splits into lines, and counts lines starting with '+' or '-' but not '+++' or '---'.

claims.text: A pure add or remove counts its whole body; an in-place edit counts only the lines that moved.
claims.why: A pure add/remove produces a unified diff where all added/removed lines are +/- lines; an in-place edit produces only the changed lines as +/- lines. The count reflects that.

claims.text: Map of {symbol name -> diff magnitude} for symbols whose extracted source differs, plus pure adds/removes.
claims.why: The function builds before_map and after_map from extract_units and includes any name where before_srcs != after_srcs, which naturally includes pure adds/removes.

claims.text: Matched by NAME against a (name -> sorted source list) map rather than a single name->source dict, so duplicate names (same-named methods on sibling classes, nested closures) don't silently clobber each other and under-report a real change.
claims.why: The function uses before_map and after_map as dict[str, list[str]] and compares sorted lists; duplicate names accumulate sources and are compared as lists, so changes to any occurrence are detected.

claims.text: A file with no language spec (unsupported extension) contributes nothing -- there is no unit-level ground truth to diff, only whole-file text, and this module deliberately doesn't fall back to that (a whole-file "changed" label would be far too coarse to be an honest must_include).
claims.why: The function returns {} if spec_for(rel) is None, before any extraction.

claims.text: The magnitude is only ever used for cap-ranking in _mint_from_diffs; it plays no part in WHETHER a symbol counts as changed (that's the != comparison below).
claims.why: The changed dict is populated only when before_srcs != after_srcs; magnitude is computed only for those and used later only in ranking.

claims.text: The scope membership test -- ``rel in modules`` -- exactly as slice.py uses it for its own neighborhood expansion (slice.py, ``rel not in modules`` around line 225).
claims.why: The function returns frozenset(idx.get("modules") or {}), which matches the described membership test, but slice.py's usage is outside this chunk.

claims.text: Degrades to an empty scope (so callers mint nothing rather than crash) on ANY indexing failure -- minting must never raise on a caller looping over commits, same contract as _git.
claims.why: The function wraps cached_index in try/except Exception and returns frozenset() on any exception.

claims.text: ``files`` keys not present in ``in_scope`` are excluded from BOTH target and label consideration entirely -- they never reach ``_diffed_symbols`` at all, so an out-of-scope file that would raise/misbehave under unit-level parsing (a minified bundle, say) can never even get that far.
claims.why: The function computes skipped = [rel for rel in files if rel not in in_scope] and then scoped = {rel: v for rel, v in files.items() if rel in in_scope}; only scoped files are passed to _diffed_symbols.

claims.text: ``diagnostics["skipped_out_of_scope"]`` is always present (sorted, maybe empty).
claims.why: skipped is sorted and assigned to diagnostics['skipped_out_of_scope'] at the start.

claims.text: ``diagnostics["reason"]`` is present only when ``task`` is ``None``
claims.why: In every branch that returns None, diagnostics['reason'] is set; the successful path does not set 'reason'.

claims.text: The task's ``target`` ... is, among in-scope files that have at least one diffed symbol, the one that still EXISTS after the edit with the most diffed symbols, ties broken by path for determinism -- a deleted file cannot be a slice target.
claims.why: The anchor_pool is built as {rel: syms for rel, syms in (existing or per_file).items() if rel not in floor_tripped}. When existing is empty (all changed files are deleted), it falls back to per_file, which includes deleted files (scoped[rel][1] is None). Such a deleted file can then be selected as anchor, violating the 'still EXISTS' requirement. This is a real edge case, though it requires all changed files to be deleted.

claims.text: A single changed symbol in the anchor earns symbol-level precision (``target::symbol``); more than one keeps the target file-level
claims.why: The code in this chunk selects the anchor but does not show how the target string is constructed; that logic must be in the next chunk.

claims.text: ``must_include`` is every diffed symbol in every OTHER in-scope touched file (never the anchor's own), capped at MUST_INCLUDE_CAP keeping the largest-magnitude symbols (``must_include_dropped`` records how many were cut, so a capped task never silently reads as full coverage).
claims.why: The loop over per_file skips the anchor and accumulates cross_file_sizes from other files. The cap is applied as ranked[:MUST_INCLUDE_CAP] and dropped is computed. However, the final task construction and must_include_dropped field are in the next chunk; the claim about the field is uncheckable here.

claims.text: EPHEMERAL REPO ROOT -- refused before any work, for every caller.
claims.why: The function checks _is_linked_worktree(repo_root) at the top, before any other processing, and returns None with a reason if true.

claims.text: a worktree is deleted by whoever created it -- the task would be permanently unresolvable
claims.why: The reason string states this and the function returns None, preventing minting.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION ... semantic_slice's FOCUS GATE fails it closed
claims.why: The comment refers to semantic_slice's behavior, which is outside this chunk; the code does exclude floor_tripped from anchor_pool.

claims.text: Computed over ALL of per_file (not just `existing`) so a deleted-but-still-named path (e.g. a rename that trips a path-marker rule) is caught too; the content check degrades to "" for a deleted file (nothing left on disk to scan).
claims.why: The floor_tripped list is computed from per_file (which includes deleted files) and uses scoped[rel][1] or '' as the content.

claims.text: Cross-file only: a symbol NAME can repeat across files (different symbol, same name) -- keep the larger magnitude rather than letting one silently clobber the other
claims.why: The loop uses cross_file_sizes[name] = max(cross_file_sizes.get(name, 0), size).

claims.text: NOT guaranteed non-empty any more: the len(per_file) < 2 check above only guarantees at least one OTHER (non-anchor) per_file entry existed BEFORE filtering -- the junk / cross-language / secret-floor filters below can still drain every one of its symbols, so the post-filter emptiness guard after this loop is load-bearing, not defensive dead code.
claims.why: The code has an explicit `if not cross_file_sizes:` check after the loop, returning None with a reason.

claims.text: JUNK / CROSS-LANGUAGE / SECRET-FLOOR filtering (see module docstring) happens per (file, name) occurrence, BEFORE the max-magnitude merge -- a name filtered out of one file's occurrence can still be kept from another (matching-family, non-junk, non-floor-tripping) file's occurrence.
claims.why: The loop processes each (rel, name) individually, applies the filters before updating cross_file_sizes, and the max merge only happens for names that pass all filters.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION ... semantic_slice withholds this file as a neighbour in EVERY lane, so any symbol defined only here can never appear in any slice -- keeping it in must_include would be a guaranteed, permanent miss mislabeled as a slicer defect, not a real signal.
claims.why: The comment refers to semantic_slice's behavior; the code does skip floor_tripped files in the label loop, which is consistent.

claims.text: Label hygiene filtered every cross-file candidate -- see CROSS-FILE ONLY in the module docstring: minting must_include=[] here would be exactly as vacuous (harness._recall's 1.0-for-empty) as the single-file case already guarded above, just reached by a different path. Diagnostics carry what was filtered even though there is no task dict to carry it on, so the drop is reported, never silent.
claims.why: The code sets diagnostics['labels_filtered_junk'], etc., and returns None with a reason when cross_file_sizes is empty.

observations.what: anchor_pool falls back to per_file when existing is empty, which can include deleted files as anchors, contradicting the docstring requirement that the target must still exist.

_diffed_symbols uses before_text or '' and after_text or '', which makes a deleted file indistinguishable from an empty file in terms of extraction; this is intentional for the diff but could affect pure-delete detection.

The MUST_INCLUDE_CAP is applied as ranked[:MUST_INCLUDE_CAP] and dropped is computed; the kept list is sorted alphabetically, not by magnitude, but the ranking for selection is by magnitude. This is fine.
The diagnostics dict always includes 'skipped_secret_floor' even when empty; the docstring does not explicitly promise it, but it is present.

The cross_file_sizes loop does not skip files with rel_lang None before the language-family check; such files contribute to labels_filtered_cross_language. This is consistent with the comment but could be surprising if a file has no spec and a non-junk name.
